(per Hon'ble Smt Justice K.Sujana) Heard Sri Venkata Sai Krishna Ponnuru, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Godugu Mallesham, learned Assistant Government Pleader representing learned Advocate General appearing for the respondents.
2.

This writ petition is filed challenging the impugned detention order dated 04.08.2023 passed by the Commissioner of Police, Rachakonda Commissionerate-2nd respondent, vide proceedings No.37/PD-CELL/RCKD/2023 under Section (2) of Section 3 of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Boot-leggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders,
Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1 of 1986 (Amendment Act No.13 of 2018) (for short 'Act No.1 of 1986'), is being illegal, KL,J &SKS,J Wp No.24462 2023 arbitrary, unconstitutional and against the principles of natural justice.
3. The detenu is the son of writ petitioner and studying BBA at Pragathi Maha Vidyalaya College and he is attending college regularly.

entities.text: Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Boot-leggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: On 08.06.2023 the petitioner was informed that her son was arrested and on 13.06.2023, the detenu was remanded to judicial custody by registering a case in Cr.No.201 of 2023 for the offence under Section 392 of IPC which is illegal.
As such, prayed the Court to set aside the detention order passed by the 2nd respondent declaring it as illegal.

4. The 2nd respondent passed the detention order dated 04.08.2023 against the detenu under Section 3 (2) r/w.Section 2 (g) of the Act No.1 of 1986, alleging that the activities of detenu are creating large scale fear and panic among the general public especially women and thus pre-judicial to the public order and affected society adversely.

sentences.text:
The impugned detention order was passed by the 2nd respondent relying on the following crimes :
KL,J &SKS,J Wp No.24462 2023 6.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the impugned order is passed without application of mind.

The detaining authority did not consider the entire material properly including the nature of allegations leveled against the detenu and further he is a student and studying BBA and attending college KL,J &SKS,J Wp No.24462 2023 regularly.
The offence alleged to have committed by the detenu do not disturb public order and at best would be a law and order problem.
The detaining authority did not consider all the said aspects and there is no subjective satisfaction arrived by him while issuing impugned detention order.
Therefore, the impugned detention order is liable to be set aside.

7. On the other hand, learned Assistant Government Pleader appearing for the respondents would submit that the allegations leveled against the detenu are serious in nature and he is involved in similar crimes again and again, creating panic and scare among the public in an organized way not only under the limits of Rachakonda Police Commissionerate but also in Malakpet jurisdiction, he is acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of 'public order' thereby disturbing public peace and the individual is in the habit of committing crimes again and again.
Therefore, he is not entitled to any equitable consideration and if the detenu is released from detention, he may indulge in similar crimes disturbing the 'public order'.

8. A perusal of the detention order dated 04.08.2023 it is seen that the 2nd respondent relying on four crimes, one of which is Cr.No.93 of 2023 under Section 392 of IPC of Bibinagar P.S., KL,J &SKS,J Wp No.24462 2023 wherein the detenue robbed gold chain (pusthelathadu) by using criminal force under the point of threat and escaped with stolen booty weighing about 4.00 tulas and stolen booty worth Rs.80,000/-.

In Cr.No.197 of 2023 filed under Section 379 r/w.Section 511 of IPC, wherein when the victim was on the way to Kirana shop, at about 10.40 hours, detenu along with other person went on bike from back side of victim and attempted to rob her gold pusthelathadu forcefully from her neck, in Cr.No.487 of 2023 filed under Section 379 of IPC the detenu committed theft of Honda Hornet which was parked in front of the house of the complainant.

In Cr.No.201 of 2023 filed under Section 392 of IPC, the detenu snatched gold pusthelathadu weighing about 4.5 tulas from the neck of the wife of the complainant when she along with her baby was walking on the road and also dragged her up to 10 yards.

Apart from the above crimes, the detenu is involved in Cr.No.185 of 2023 filed under Section 379 of IPC of Malakpet P.S.
9.
The allegation leveled against the detenu in another crime is snatching of gold pusthelathadu of women.

According to the detaining authority the detenue has been engaging himself in unlawful acts and indulging in committing of robberies, property theft and snatching of Mangalasutras from women folk by using criminal force on public road in broad day light continuously,
KL,J &SKS,J Wp No.24462 2023 repeatedly not only in Rachakonda Commissionerate but also in the jurisdiction of Malakpet P.S.
The said acts of detenu has been creating large scale fear and panic among the general public especially women folk.

According to him, the detenu committed four crimes in quick Smt. Gyara Premalatha vs The State Of Telangana on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26694663/

sentences.text: Therefore, he has arrived at the subjective satisfaction that the illegal acts of the detenu involve breach of peace and public tranquility and that his continuous presence in the area is detrimental to the maintenance of 'public order' apart from disturbing peace, tranquility and social harmony in the society, therefore, passed the alleged detention order.
10. The detention order would reveal that the detenu was involved in another crime apart from subject crimes.

The allegations leveled against the detenue are grave in nature and he is involved in similar crimes, habitually engaging himself in unlawful acts and indulging in committing of robberies, property theft offences and gold chain snatching including sacred mangalsutras from women folk by using criminal force on public roads in broad day light and in one of the crime, the detenu dragged a woman with baby and committing offences repeatedly, thereby creating large scale fear and panic among the general public especially women.

His intention is to earn easy money to KL,J &SKS,J Wp No.24462 2023 live lavish life, though he is a student involved in illegal acts detrimental to the maintenance of public order apart from disturbing peace, tranquility and social harmony in the society.

11. Thus, modus operandi adopted by the detenu to earn easy money by committing robberies and theft and pursuant to the confession made by the detenu police seized Rs.40,000/- towards his share in Cr.No.93 of 2023 and in Cr.No.487 of 2023 they seized Honda Hornet bearing No.TS 09 EV 5218 and in Cr.No.201 of 2023 the police seized stolen booty i.e., gold Mangalsutra and even the stolen booty in Cr.No.185 of 2023 of 2023 are seized.

The detaining authority considering that the detenu was involved in series of property offences and if he is released, he may commit similar offences in his limits in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of 'public order' arrived at a conclusion that his act prejudicial to the maintenance of 'public order' and accordingly passed the detention order against the detenu.
Thus, the acts committed by the detenu would certainly disturb the 'public order'.
12. The acts committed by the detenu come under the category of 'goonda'.

The object of the Act No.1 of 1986 is to provide for preventive detention of Bootleggers, Dacoits etc. including 'Goonda'.
Section - 2 (g) of the Act No.1 of 1986

defines "Goonda", which means a person, who either by himself or as a member of or KL,J &SKS,J Wp No.24462 2023 leader of a gang, habitually commits,
or attempts to commit or abets the commission of offences punishable under Chapter - XVI or Chapter - XVII or Chapter XXII of the IPC.

entities.text: Chapter - XVI or Chapter - XVII or Chapter XXII
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: 13. While passing the detention order, the detaining authority not only considered the commission of offences committed by the detenu and his associates, but also considered its impact disturbing 'public order' and also the modus operandi adopted by them in commission of offences.

Therefore,
in order to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences, the impugned detention order was passed.
14. It is not in dispute that the detaining authority shall consider the nature of offence and the manner in which it was committed.
He has to consider the entire material on record and come to a subjective satisfaction while issuing detention order.

The detaining authority has to draw a Smt. Gyara Premalatha vs The State Of Telangana on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26694663/
3 distinction between 'law and order' and 'public order'.
15.

sentences.text: In the present case, the detaining authority on consideration of the entire material arrived at the subjective satisfaction with regard to causing disturbance to the 'public order' on account of the acts committed by the detenu.
There are grave allegations against him, so also modus operandi adopted by him, and the acts committed by him certainly disturb the public order.
KL,J &SKS,J Wp No.24462 2023 16.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ashok Kumar v. Delhi Administration 1 observed that preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society.
The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing.

17. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar 2, the Apex Court held as under:
"...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some?

entities.text: Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them.
Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder.
Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder.
When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder.
They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order.
Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions.
The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder.
Other examples can be imagined.
The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large.
A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defence of India Act but disturbances which subvert the public order are.

A District Magistrate is . (1982) 2 SCC 403 . AIR 1966 SC 740 KL,J &SKS,J Wp No.24462 2023 entitled to take action under Rule 30(1)(b) to prevent subversion of public order but not in aid of maintenance of law and order under ordinary circumstances.

It will thus appear that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order".
One has to imagine three concentric circles.
Law and order represents the largest circle within which is the next circle representing public order and the smallest circle represents security of State.

It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State."
18.

As seen from the above judgment and the detention order, the detaining authority considered the entire material on record and came to a subjective satisfaction that the acts committed by the detenu, the nature of offence and the manner in which it was committed are disturbing the public order.

To prevent the detenu from committing similar offences, the detaining authority shall issue Smt. Gyara Premalatha vs The State Of Telangana on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26694663/
4 preventive detention order against the detenu.
19. The detenu committed four crimes of chain snatching and attempted to snatch a gold chain and theft of vehicle and he is engaged in unlawful activities by committing the said property offences and snatching of gold chains, thereby acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of 'public order'
as it disturbs peace, tranquility in the society.

sentences.text: Further, the police also seized gold ornaments and bike pertaining to the subject cases.
KL,J &SKS,J Wp No.24462 2023 20.
In view of the acts committed by the detenu it would certainly create large scale panic in general more particularly women folk.
All the said cases were considered by the detaining authority while passing detention order.

Therefore, viewed from any angle we are of the considered view that there is no error in the impugned detention order dated 04.08.2023 passed by the 2nd respondent and the consequential approval order passed by the 1st respondent vide G.O.Rt.No.1104 General Administration (Spl.Law & Order) Deptt., dated 05.08.2023 respectively.
Hence, there are no merits in the writ petition and the same is liable to be dismissed.
21. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous applications, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.
